verdict.rationale: Recurly documents usage-based billing through consumption-driven add-ons on subscription plans, which gives a hybrid subscription-plus-usage model. It also supports subscription quantity and price adjustments and issues credit invoices. The pack says nothing about tiered, volume, or graduated pricing schemes, prepaid commitments, or overage handling, and does not show the setup is no-code. Missing for 10: tiered, volume and graduated pricing evidence, commitments/prepaid drawdown, overage pricing, explicit no-code configuration, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a finance lead, I can price with tiered, volume, graduated, per-unit, and hybrid subscription-plus-usage models — including credits, commitments, and overage — without custom code

citations.quote: Usage-based billing lets you define consumption-driven add-ons, track measured units across plans, and charge at the end of every billing cycle
Recurly's usage-based billing model lets you charge customers at the end of each billing cycle based on their actual consumption
Modify a subscription's plan, price, quantity, or add-ons in Recurly — with control over timing, proration behavior, credits, charges, discounts, and trial handling.
Credit invoices give every credit its own distinct invoice — separate from charge invoices.
